LESSON: GRAPHIC DESIGN - TYPOGRAPHY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: FINE ARTS
Strand: Multimedia Arts (2D Art)
Topic 2.1: Graphic Design - Typography
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Graphic Design - Typography, part of Multimedia Arts (2D Art) in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 FINE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why should one use a slanted tip when improvising a calligraphy pen? 2. What influences artist choice of typographic style?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Graphic Design - Typography together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication: as the learner engagingly discusses the concept of typography.

● Imagination and Creativity: as the learner generates new ideas when illustrating calligraphic text for the

seasonal card

● Digital literacy: as the learner manipulates digital tools to design letters and write words.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner improvises calligraphy pens to write calligraphy

● Self-efficacy: as the learner displays, critiques others’ works while reflecting on own graphic illustrations.

31

Values:
● Integrity: as the learner fairly critiques others’ works.

● Patriotism: as the learner write messages inspired by civic education.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Internet, ICT devices, sample video demonstration on calligraphy, sample calligraphy/graffiti works, papers,

approved books, adapted brushes with grip, pencils/pens grip, adapted digital devices, page turners, universal cuffs,

multipurpose communication board text-to-speech software, footboard,

Other Related Service Providers:

Resource person, Speech Therapist , Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist,
